title: Can a single photon start a camera?

segments.text: Can a single photon start a camera?
A photon lands on a MOS capacitor inside a CCD and creates electrons at the semiconductor‑oxide interface.
The capacitor is biased above the inversion threshold, so each photon generates charge proportional to the light intensity.
The control circuit nudges that charge into the neighboring capacitor, repeating the hand‑off across the array.
When the last capacitor receives the packet, a charge amplifier converts it to a voltage pulse.
That voltage becomes the digital data we later see on screen, all because of a single photon.
